request: One of the long edges of the blade does not have a radius. Add radius to that long edge R=0,635cm

actions.target: The unrounded longitudinal edge of the oblique crossing arm, located on F001 along the long planar side wall FACE 21 and opposite the existing radius-6.350 mm continuous rounded shaft wall FACE 20.
actions.relational_constraint: The target must be the continuous sharp longitudinal boundary of the blade-like oblique arm R01. Select the edge chain associated with FACE 21 and the elongated planar shaft faces FACE 17 and FACE 19, on the side opposite the already rounded cylindrical wall FACE 20. Do not modify the end edges, bore edges, transverse-hole edges, central pivot-bore edges, or the localized transition geometry.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify which long edge of the blade is currently unrounded. The available face topology localizes it to the sharp longitudinal edge chain of F001 adjacent to FACE 21; exact CadQuery EDGE indices were not supplied in model.json and must be resolved by face adjacency and edge length during implementation.
steps: Isolate section R01, the oblique crossing arm represented by SOLID 0. Do not alter the orthogonal crossing arm R02 or the central clamp and pivot housing R03.
Convert the specified radius from 0,635 cm to the model units: 6.350 mm.
Use F001, the oblique structural shaft, as the parent feature for the new fillet. The arm follows the approximate longitudinal direction (0.833954, 0, 0.551833) in the CAD x-z plane.

Inspect the longitudinal boundaries of FACE 21, the long planar side wall. Identify the longest sharp edge or tangent-connected edge chain shared with the elongated planar shaft faces, principally FACE 17 and FACE 19.

Confirm that the selected chain is on the side opposite FACE 20, which is already a continuous cylindrical rounded shaft wall of radius 6.350 mm. This comparison distinguishes the missing radius from the blade edge that is already rounded.

Where the longitudinal boundary is topologically divided by the central region, collect all collinear or tangent-continuous edge segments belonging to the same physical long edge. Stop the selection at genuine terminal faces or at transition boundaries that cannot support the requested radius.

Exclude every circular edge belonging to FACE 0, FACE 1, FACE 3, or FACE 15, because these are transverse-hole, end-bore, and central pivot-bore boundaries. Also exclude short edges belonging only to the localized rounded-transition feature F006.

Apply a constant-radius edge fillet of 6.350 mm to the selected longitudinal edge chain. Use tangent propagation only along the same physical blade edge; do not allow propagation onto end faces, hole rims, or the opposite already-rounded wall.

Recompute SOLID 0 and verify that the fillet replaces the sharp junction adjacent to FACE 21 with a continuous cylindrical or equivalent rolling-ball blend. The resulting blade profile should have a radius matching the existing 6.350 mm rounded long edge.

Check the full length of the new blend for self-intersection, especially where it approaches F006 and the central clamp region. If a single propagated fillet fails because the edge is split, apply the same 6.350 mm radius to the valid contiguous segments while maintaining tangency across segment junctions.
Verify that the arm remains one valid solid, that the longitudinal end bore F002 and holes F003 through F005 remain open and unchanged, and that there is no interference introduced with R02 or R03.
Regenerate the +Z, -Z, +Y, -Y, and iso1 views to confirm that the formerly sharp long blade edge now presents the same rounded treatment as the opposite long edge.

intention: Make the two long edges of the blade-like oblique arm consistently rounded with a 6.350 mm radius.
Remove the sharp longitudinal edge while preserving the arm holes, central transitions, and assembly interfaces.
